subject: Sizing sync: dedicated capacity technical deep-dive & proposed slots
messages:
From: Andrew Holt <andrew.holt@polaris-payments.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tumai Okonkwo <tumai.ops@polaris-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-discovery: sizing sync & sample data

Hannah / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today — helpful to see Redwood's runtime behavior and the options for Dedicated. Quick recap from our side and a request to lock a technical sizing call with your SE to align on throughput/latency and required inputs.

Recap (high level):
- Primary use: real-time authorization + fraud scoring pipeline (inference per txn).
- Expected steady: ~1,200 requests/sec during peak business hours.
- Avg payload: ~350 tokens; typical response size ~120 tokens.
- p50 target: <40ms; p95 target: <150ms (end-to-end inference).
- Concurrency: expect bursts up to ~40 concurrent LLM sessions; sustained concurrency around 12-18.

Can we schedule a 60-min dedicated sizing call (SE + infra) next week? Proposed slots (PST):
- Wed Dec 9 — 10:00–11:00 AM
- Thu Dec 10 — 2:00–3:00 PM
- Fri Dec 11 — 9:00–10:00 AM

I attached a simple CSV with a short sample of throughput traces and a system diagram to help your prep. On the call we'd like to cover: exact QPS profile, acceptable latency SLOs, expected request size distribution, and how Redwood would size a dedicated GPU pool + fallback plan.

If you need anything else before the call (logs, auth patterns, or test tokens), let me know.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Holt
Head of Engineering — Platform
Polaris Payments
Attachments: polaris_service_diagram.pdf (PDF), polaris_throughput_sample.csv (CSV)

Hi Andrew — great to meet you on the call yesterday, and thanks for the attachments.

We can definitely run a dedicated sizing deep-dive. dev_patel (SE) and I will join to run through the workload profile and recommend a configuration. Based on the numbers you shared, we may want to run a short pre-call validation of the sample traces — that helps us size peak buffer and KV cache strategy.

Of the slots you proposed, current team availability is:
- Wed Dec 9 — 10:00–11:00 AM PST — OK for us (preferred)
- Thu Dec 10 — 2:00–3:00 PM PST — tentative (another meeting for Marissa)
- Fri Dec 11 — 9:00–10:00 AM PST — OK but later in the day works better for our east-coast infra folks.

If Dec 9 at 10:00 AM PST works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda:
Agenda (60 min):
1) Quick recap & goals (5 min)
2) Workload & traffic profile deep-dive (15 min)
3) Latency SLOs / failure modes (10 min)
4) Dedicated pool sizing recommendations (20 min)
5) Next steps / PoC plan (10 min)

Please confirm the Dec 9 slot and any additional attendees on your side. Also confirm if the sample CSV contains the most representative traces or if there’s a larger dump you can share (S3 link or direct upload).

— Hannah

Andrew / team — quick note from the SE side on what will make the December 9 session most productive: 

Pre-call checklist (please bring / share if possible):
- Representative QPS timeline (CSV is fine) with timestamps and request size (tokens).
- A few sample payloads (sanitized) so we can validate tokenization impact.
- Target p50/p95 ground truth latency (if you have application-side numbers).
- Any constraints on GPU types or regions (e.g., must be us-west-2).

On the call I’ll:
- Walk through how we translate QPS + token distribution into GPU pool sizing (batching + KV cache effect).
- Share latency/cost tradeoffs for quantized variants and fallback routing.
- Propose an initial Dedicated config (pool size, queueing thresholds, burst guardrails).

Estimated deliverables after the call: a one-page sizing recommendation + a follow-up runbook for a short validation PoC.

If Dec 9 10:00 AM PST is final, I’ll reserve the slot in my calendar and request access to the CSV (or an S3 link) so I can pre-run an estimate.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
